title: Nothing's Free
coreMove: Name the emotional fee before you buy the return.
sourcePressure: Good returns charge a price, often volatility, discomfort, doubt, and regret rather than an explicit invoice.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Acting as if fees only mean visible charges or fund expenses.

hook: opening with a generic paycheck scene
opening with a moral lesson about discipline
opening Nothing's Free with a swapped-in personal finance anecdote
counterintuition: reducing Nothing's Free to common-sense advice
tryThisNow: write down your values for ninety seconds
asking for a generic money reflection instead of the fee move
examples: reusing visible anchors from adjacent chapters instead of fee and volatility

exampleSpecs.domain: a young investor choosing an equity allocation after watching a drawdown simulation
exampleSpecs.audience: a saver who wants returns without feeling the fee
exampleSpecs.stakes: panic selling would turn a good asset into a bad personal fit
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she watches a simulated account drop by a year's salary and names whether she can still hold it
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a brokerage simulator showing a red six-figure drop

exampleSpecs.domain: a cattle rancher buying drought insurance with an ugly premium
exampleSpecs.audience: a rancher accepting an explicit cost to avoid a hidden ruin cost
exampleSpecs.stakes: resenting the premium may ignore the price of sleeping through dry months
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he signs the policy after placing the premium beside the cost of forced herd liquidation
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a policy packet beside a cattle count written on a feed-store receipt

exampleSpecs.domain: a novelist turning down a guaranteed advance for a riskier royalty deal
exampleSpecs.audience: a writer naming the emotional price of upside
exampleSpecs.stakes: the royalty path includes years of doubt that may be unbearable
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she writes the worst plausible royalty statement before choosing the contract
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a contract offer next to a blank royalty projection sheet

exampleSpecs.domain: a restaurant owner keeping menu prices flexible despite customer complaints
exampleSpecs.audience: an owner learning that pricing freedom costs discomfort
exampleSpecs.stakes: avoiding complaints may quietly destroy margins
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she reads three complaint emails aloud, then compares them with the supplier bill increase they pay for
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a supplier invoice beside printed customer emails

exampleSpecs.domain: a mountain guide charging clients for weather cancellation reserves
exampleSpecs.audience: a guide explaining that safety margins are part of the fee
exampleSpecs.stakes: clients may resent paying for days when nothing happens
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after canceling a climb, he shows the reserve fund that lets guides make the safe call
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a weather bulletin clipped to a guide roster

exampleSpecs.domain: a family keeping a boring bond ladder while friends celebrate hot returns
exampleSpecs.audience: a household accepting envy as the fee for stability
exampleSpecs.stakes: chasing excitement could destroy the calm the portfolio is meant to buy
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: they write the emotion they are paying with when friends brag at dinner
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a brokerage statement folded beside an invitation to dinner
